identity.title: Kinematic signatures of a low-mass planet with a moderately inclined orbit in a protoplanetary disk
identity.journal: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan

paper_type_evidence.quote: We investigated the features induced by the planet with an inclined orbit through three-dimensional hydrodynamic simulations.
Figure [13](#fig:maps) shows the part of the channel maps for $^{12}$CO , $^{13}$CO, and C$^{18}$O, for the disks of HD 163296, which is provided by MAPS (cite: MAPS1).

question.value: Can a low-mass planet on a moderately inclined orbit produce kinematic (velocity-kink) features in CO channel maps as prominent as a massive coplanar planet, and how do these differ across CO isotopologues?

evidence.quote: We found that a smaller planet, with the inclination being $\sim 10^{\circ}$ – $20^{\circ}$, can produce kinematic features as prominent as those induced by the massive coplanar planet.
This paper uses the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA#2018.1.01055.L.
we considered the rotation transition in $J=2-1$ of $^{12}$CO  and its isotopologues $^{13}$CO  and C$^{18}$O.
for the disks of HD 163296, which is provided by MAPS (cite: MAPS1).

findings_qualitative.value: Inclined-planet features fade for rarer isotopologues, whereas a coplanar massive planet gives neck and gap structures in 13CO and C18O

evidence.quote: In the case of the inclined planet, the kinematic features is fainter for rarer isotopologues

findings_qualitative.value: Planets in the back layer produce much weaker features, so only about half of such planets are detectable

evidence.quote: only half the planets are detectable

claims.hypothesis: A smaller inclined planet can produce kinematic features as clear as a massive coplanar planet
claims.experiment: 3D hydro plus RADMC3D channel maps for various Mp and i_orb
claims.result: Mp/M*=3e-4 at 10-20 deg gives 12CO features comparable to the coplanar Mp/M*=2e-3 case
claims.finding: Inclination can reduce the mass discrepancy between gap and kink estimates

evidence.quote: the smaller planet ($M_{\rm p}/M_{\ast}= 3\times 10^{-4}$) can make the kinematic features as clear as that induced by the coplanar massive planet

claims.hypothesis: Isotopologue dependence distinguishes inclined from coplanar planets
claims.result: Rarer isotopologues show weak or no features for the inclined planet, but neck and gap structures for the coplanar planet
claims.finding: 13CO and C18O observations can decide the orbital inclination

evidence.loc: 3.5 Comparison with the case with the coplanar planet
evidence.quote: the observations of C$^{18}$O can be decisive to determine the orbital inclination of the planet.

claims.hypothesis: The HD 163296 kinks are due to inclined or coplanar planets
claims.experiment: Compared MAPS maps with the simulated features
claims.result: Outer kink at 220 au lacks 13CO/C18O features; inner kink at 67 au has neck and gap structures
claims.finding: Outer kink is consistent with an inclined planet, inner kink with a coplanar planet

evidence.quote: We concluded that the kink observed at 220 au can be induced by the inclined planet, while the kink at 67 au is consistent to that induced by the coplanar planet.

limitations_admitted.value: Temperature in the radiative transfer is inconsistent with the locally isothermal hydrodynamics; the inner boundary may cause artifacts; the tail feature may come from the unresolved circumplanetary disk

evidence.loc: 3.5 Comparison with the case with the coplanar planet
evidence.quote: this tail structure can be the artifact caused by the unresolved circumplanetary disk.
The orbital inclination is damped due to disk–planet interaction; however, we did not consider this in our paper.

referee_caveats_inferred: Comparison with HD 163296 is qualitative and visual, with no quantitative fit
The locally isothermal EOS and fixed CO abundance affect emission-layer heights
Low vertical resolution; only one snapshot at 100 orbits
Inclination damping is ignored, so persistence of the inclination is unproven

data_public_as_stated.value: MAPS data used for comparison; the ALMA project code is acknowledged

evidence.quote: This paper uses the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA#2018.1.01055.L.

reproducibility.estimated_data_volume_inferred: Small for ALMA (MAPS cubes, tens of GB); the simulations dominate the cost
reproducibility.score_reason: Simulation setup is well described and the codes are public, but the ALMA comparison is only qualitative and the parameter table and input files are missing.
reproducibility.rediscovery_reason: The results are mostly qualitative simulation morphology, and the ALMA part is a visual comparison.
